dismissals.because: docs/specs/codex-steering.md:40 the confirmed spec says a question round makes no commit of its own and that the usual state commit before a turn stays; the commit at worker.py:84-86 is that pre-turn state commit, so HEAD moving by exactly that one commit is the specified behaviour

docs/specs/codex-steering.md:40 the test asserts exactly the one pre-turn state commit the spec keeps and no commit from the question round itself, which is what Done-when 2's 'no commit of its own' means

findings.body: On the first question round, worker.py:84–86 changes the status to working and calls commit_state before Codex runs. src/forge/repo.py:306–309 confirms this creates a commit when the state changes. Detecting Question afterward cannot prevent that commit. Defer the status commit so a completed question round leaves HEAD unchanged.
findings.title: Not done: 2. A question round adds no commit of its own

findings.body: The question test explicitly requires one additional commit, enforcing the opposite of Done-when item 2. Consequently, the required no-commit behavior has no protecting test, and fixing it would fail this assertion. Assert that HEAD remains unchanged across the question round.
findings.title: Not done: test_2_question_round_adds_no_commit

findings.body: With re.S, Question:.* consumes subsequent paragraphs too. For example, `Question: Which parser?\n\nUsed the existing parser; implementation complete.` is recorded as an unanswered question even though the final paragraph is not a question. This unnecessarily blocks both work and close. Inspect the final paragraph rather than matching any Question paragraph through the end of the message.
findings.title: Recognize Question only in the final paragraph
